newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Crippled Congo traders press Kabila to open border.
newsitem.headline: Crippled Congo traders press Kabila to open border.

text.p: Dozens of handicapped traders rolled their wheelchairs up to the gates of President Laurent Kabila's residence on Saturday to demand the reopening of the Democratic Republic of Congo's border.

"Since the border was closed we have not even had enough money to give our children a little bread," Bofengo Bavon, vice- president of the traders' association, told Reuters. He was born with malformed limbs.

The handicapped have for years profited from a loophole in regulations which allowed them cut-rate customs duties on importing goods from Brazzaville, the capital of neighbouring Congo, three km (two miles) across the Congo river.
Officially the border has been closed since Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo entered Kinshasa a fortnight ago after a seven-month bush war.
